_comment: Maps non-infantry unit name keys to the art that draws them. A key can be an exact tiered name ('Medium Tank III') or a bare family name used as the catch-all for every tier that has no more specific entry ('Artillery'). Standard infantry is discovered automatically from infantry_<year>.png files in the culture folders: the file with the greatest year not later than the unit's year is used. Anything not covered here falls back to the classic art.
_comment_variants: A key's value is either one entry or a list of them. Each entry is either a plain filename (applies to whichever country asks) or an object {'file': ..., 'countries': [...]} restricted to those country ids -- the exact strings that key data/json/countries_data.json, e.g. 'Germany', 'German Reich', 'German Empire'. A country matching one of the restricted entries sees that picture; everyone else falls through to the first unrestricted entry for that key and eventually to classic. Standard infantry uses the filename-driven rule described above instead of manifest variants. See map_logic/rendering/symbol_loader.py for the exact matching and fallback rules.
_comment_cultures: Culture groups allow reusing common country sets. In a 'countries' field, use either a culture group name (string) or a list of country ids (array). Example: 'countries': 'germanic' or 'countries': ['Germany', 'France'].
_comment_folders: 'file' paths are relative to this style's folder and may include a subfolder -- images here are organized into one subfolder per culture group (e.g. 'french/Char_B1_bis.png') and the loader uses that folder for country-scoped entries. Infantry filenames drop their culture prefix (e.g. 'infantry_1914.png' rather than 'french_infantry_1914.png') since the subfolder already says which culture it is. The first folder below the style folder must match a name in '_cultures'.
